parts.t: RECIPE 04 — The grader that marks its own homework until it passes
From: Claude Killed My Social Media (30M+ Views, 90% Automated) · 22 Jul 2026 · 17:57 · watch
Read this first
Most of this video is her own product again. Blotato, $29/month, connecting social accounts. You do not post to social media as a business, so nearly all of it is not for you.
But one idea inside it is something you already do for products and have never done for words. That is the whole recipe.
THE IDEA — a writing gate that refuses to publish
She does not ask Claude to "write a good post". She makes it grade its own work against a fixed rubric and rewrite until it passes.
"The post grader uses a viral rubric to determine the virality of your post, and it's going to keep iterating on your post until it passes a certain score or a certain grade."
You already have this — for PDFs
release_check.py refuses to let a product go out if it fails. Nothing refuses your listing copy.
This video is that same idea, pointed at sentences.
Her actual pre-publish rules — copy these, they cost nothing
"No M dashes, no banned words, using active voice and contractions for viral copywriting. No hashtags because it's Twitter... And then under the character limit."
No em dashes
the single clearest AI tell
A banned-words list
hers is long; this is a "starting point"
Active voice + contractions
reads human, not corporate
Platform-specific hashtag rule
"I only want hashtags on Instagram and TikTok"
Under the character limit
mechanical, checkable
Every one of those is checkable by a plain script. No AI needed to enforce them.
Her three hook frameworks — she writes all three, then picks
Watching it work on a real post, it produced:
Receipts
"30 million views in 30 days"
Reverse hook
"everyone says pick one platform, I pick six"
Specific numbers
"Six platforms, 30 days, 30 million views"
It chose the reverse hook "because it's polarizing and we're posting on Twitter."
Three drafts against three named frameworks, then a reasoned pick. That is transferable to an Etsy title, a product description, anything.
The working habit worth stealing — the screenshot folder
"Throughout the week, you just take photos or screenshots of cool stuff. You drop it into a folder.
And then when you sit down to make content, you tell Claude, 'Hey, go analyze all of the photos and screenshots I took throughout the week and let's make content out of them.'"
Collect all week without thinking. Make things in one sitting. Costs nothing, needs no tool.
One small prompt detail worth keeping
When putting text on an image for vertical video:
"respecting social media safe zones for short-form vertical content"
"This is really important because if you don't do this, then it's going to add text way too close to the edges, and it just looks weird."
A five-word phrase that prevents a whole class of ugly output.
What to try — free, and it points at your real business
Do not build her social system. Build the gate, for your listings.

You already discovered today that two of your listings made claims the product did not deliver — a title page promising 540 meanings that delivered none, and a description saying 25 pages when the file held 23.
A pre-publish word gate is the thing that catches that class of error.
ALSO MENTIONED — kept, not tidied
The five-skill pack she gives away: content coach (an orchestrator that decides what
to do), brand brief (one-time setup, asks about your voice and offers), post writer, post grader, post scheduler.
Installed by typing "Import these skills into this project" — she says it takes about 5 minutes, and Claude Code needs a restart after
She organises work as one project per purpose, each connected to GitHub —
"all of my changes are saved"
Her pricing aside: 20 social accounts on Buffer would be "over $80 per month"
Her claim that third-party publishing does not hurt reach is **her own product's
selling point**, and she is the only source for it here
